subsections.title: Aliases & Disposable Email
subsections.summary: Keep your real address out of sign-up forms.

blocks.html: Use an alias for accounts you’ll keep — it forwards to your inbox and can be switched off if it starts getting spam. Use a disposable inbox only for one-off sign-ups you never need again.

blocks.label: Careful
blocks.html: Many disposable inboxes are public: anyone who types the same address can read the mail. Never use one for an account you care about — whoever uses that address next could reset your password.

subsections.title: Run Your Own Email
subsections.summary: Self-hosted mail servers — and why it’s hard.

blocks.html: Running your own mail server gives you full control, but it is one of the hardest things to self-host. Big providers reject mail without correct SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, new servers often land on blocklists, and many home internet providers block the ports email needs. DIY Mail is an honest look at what it takes. If you just want your own domain, a host like Migadu or MXroute is far easier.
